observation.what_happens: A green block hangs from a vertical spring fixed to a support above, starting from a stretched low position just above a striped bar. It is released and then oscillates vertically up and down as the spring contracts and extends.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.9 s vertical oscillation about ~110 pixels with peaks falling from 228 to ~145 pixels while x stays at noise, confirming straight-line damped oscillation. On Earth in air we expect viscous loss, so candidates go from ideal harmonic to viscous, to speed-squared air drag, to damped plus cubic spring nonlinearity.

critique.finding: The block wobbles around {s_eq} with pace {w}, slight cubic bend {alpha} and steady dry rub {mu}. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a slow drift in its misses.
critique.headline: Spring block wobbles with dry rub, only partly explained
critique.revision_idea: Add linear viscous damping alongside the dry Coulomb rub. The misses drift steadily from low to high with near-perfect autocorrelation, showing the fade is part speed-driven rather than purely constant rub.
critique.why_it_won: It keeps the cubic stiffening while using constant dry rub rather than speed-based drag, following the even shrinking of the swings more closely.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction proportional to the sign of velocity to the spring force. The bin means march steadily from negative to positive with near-perfect persistence, pointing to an unmodeled constant opposing force that shifts the oscillation center.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a lopsided spring with dry friction. Missed: the dry friction was found, but a cubic stiffness was written where the spring was lopsided.
finding: The block wobbles around about 115 px with pace about 7.6 rad/s, slight cubic bend about -0.0012 1/(px² s²) and steady dry rub about 227 px/s². It only partly captures the motion, leaving a slow drift in its misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - motion inferred from few stills, no frame-by-frame timing available
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass on spring about equilibrium is a damped Duffing oscillator: acceleration equals -w^2 times displacement from s_eq minus gamma times velocity minus alpha times cubic displacement, filmed from side so pixel position follows that 1D motion

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605123). The round was named in 493e869 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 8337791 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit edb5c02 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in 3636e41. Missed. The drawn law was a lopsided (asymmetric) spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and no drive. The referee asked for dry friction and Muse Wonder wrote a cubic spring with dry friction only: the friction came out at 0.31 ± 0.05 m/s² against the drawn 0.30, but the stiffness term is cubic (and softening) where the drawn one is quadratic, so the term set differs. It misses the unseen frames by 78 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

k2.rule: k2 A / k uniform in [0.2, 0.45], stiffer stretched (drawn 0.353)

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 13.09); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner: linear (ω), cubic α = −0.00118 ± 0.00018 (6.6σ, present), Coulomb μ (6.0σ, present); drawn: linear, quadratic (lopsided), Coulomb. Term sets differ.

spectrumAtScoring.summary: Residual spectrum of “Damped nonlinear spring” on the fitted frames (its misses, fitted as sinusoids one at a time, strongest first): strongest at ω = 1.37 rad/s (period 4.574 s), amplitude 54.4 × the noise (7.76 px in s); next at ω = 14.20 rad/s (period 0.442 s), amplitude 25.8 × the noise (3.68 px in s): 2× the motion's own frequency, a harmonic of the motion (expected for a nonlinear spring), not evidence of a drive. The motion's own frequency is 7.21 rad/s.
